result.summary: Enables the `-Wunused` compiler warning flag in CMake and silences resulting compiler warnings across the codebase. Across over 130 files, unused parameters are made anonymous, commented out, or tagged with `[[maybe_unused]]`, accompanied by a temporary commit adapting the minisketch subtree.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core does not enable `-Wunused` during compilation, allowing dead code and unused variables to silently accumulate. Unused parameters and variables can also mask logic bugs where values were intended to be checked or passed but were forgotten.
evidence: The author points out repeated PRs needed to clean up dead code (#35679, #35910, #35914, #35971, #36009, #36012, #36103, #36127, #36509).
The author highlights #36137 as 'an instance of what was thought to be dead code, but it'd just been forgotten to be used'.
result.scope_notes: Touches 137 files with mechanical parameter name removals and compiler annotations. Includes a temporary `[[nomerge]]` commit adjusting the `src/minisketch` subtree until upstream changes land.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased on master following the merge of related cleanups (such as #36275 and #36509), reducing the scope of changes from 160 files down to 137 files.
result.card: Enables the `-Wunused` warning flag in CMake and addresses all newly surfaced warnings across 137 files by removing or commenting out unused parameter names and adding `[[maybe_unused]]`. Without this warning flag, dead code accumulates and logic bugs can hide behind variables that developers forgot to use (demonstrated in #36137). The PR depends on an upstream Minisketch PR to avoid warnings in vendored code.

risk.why: A typo or accidental signature alteration while anonymizing parameters could cause compilation errors or subtle method overload resolution mismatches.
